_purpose: General order-of-magnitude ranges for flagging an extracted quantity as implausible, not for pricing. These are broad industry rules-of-thumb, not authoritative or project-specific — a value outside range means 'a human should look at this,' not 'this is wrong.' A value inside range is not proof of correctness either, just not an obvious red flag.

ranges.note: Light steel framing (residential-scale) to heavier commercial/mid-rise steel frame. Concrete or wood structures are far outside this and shouldn't be checked against it.
Typical spread/mat foundation range. Deep foundations (drilled piers into rock, like Nueces) run higher — flag, don't reject.

Pure multifamily residential only. Do NOT apply to a mixed-use building's blended GSF/unit — non-residential program area will push it outside this range for a reason that isn't an error (see Nueces: 2,147 sf/unit blended across a mosque + 36 units, not a red flag, just not a pure-residential ratio).
0 is valid and common in reduced-parking overlay districts (e.g. near a university) — don't flag 0 as an error without checking for that context first.
Roof footprint as a fraction of total GSF; low end for tall multi-story buildings, near 1.0 for single-story.
